newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hurdles lie ahead of Daewoo's U.S. car venture.
newsitem.headline: Hurdles lie ahead of Daewoo's U.S. car venture.

text.p: Daewoo Motor Co's plans to conquer the world, starting with the highly competitive U.S. market, look over-ambitious and will be difficult to achieve, analysts said on Tuesday.

"Unfavourable price conditions and virtually non-existent brand recognition will make it difficult for Daewoo to sell cars in the U.S. market," said Kim Byung-joon, an analyst at Dongwon Economic Research Institute.
Daewoo Group chairman Kim Woo-choong said on Monday Daewoo planned to re-enter the U.S. market in September with three new models, focusing mostly on sales of Leganza compact sedans.
They will be the first car sales by Daewoo Motor in the market since the company ended its partnership with General Motors Corp in 1992 over disagreements on sales strategy and investment decisions.
As part of the agreement ending its 15-year partnership, Daewoo agreed to stay out of the U.S. market through 1995.
Daewoo executives said Daewoo expected to sell 30,000 units in the United States by the end of this year and 100,000 units in 1998.
But analysts said sales of Daewoo's Leganza would not be easy as it would compete with Japanese models such as Toyota Motor Corp's Camry and Honda Motor Co's Accord.
"I don't see why U.S. consumers should be interested in Daewoo cars. I don't think there are any special things about Daewoo's technology," said Yang Dong-ki, an analyst at Dongbang Peregrine.
Sales of South Korean cars in the U.S. market in the segment for two litre engines have been poor, hampered by a low yen that makes Japanese products more competitive.
Sonata compact cars from South Korea's largest car maker, Hyundai Motor Co, a local best seller, sold only 13,321 units in the U.S. last year, down from 17,990 units.
Analysts said the high costs of setting up a sales network and after-sales service centres would cut profitability of Daewoo's U.S. car sales.
"It will take a long period of time and a lot of money to have a viable U.S. operation," said Kim of Dongwon.
Daewoo Motor said it would expand its vehicle production capacity to 2.5 million units per year by the year 2000, including overseas capacity of 1.5 million.
Daewoo has set a sales goal of 885,000 vehicles this year, including 400,000 in overseas markets, compared with last year's overall sales of 653,098 units, including 352,916 abroad.
Daewoo Motor, which earned 23 billion won ($25.7 million) in net profits in 1996 on sales of 4.3 trillion won, has set its target at 70 billion won in profits this year on sales of 6.8 trillion won.
